goal: Add an isolated local GUI extension for secure multi-provider API configuration and same-prompt comparison without persisting plaintext credentials.
acceptance_criteria: Keep the extension outside the canonical ProviderJob, evidence, packaging, and delivery authorities.
Persist provider metadata and credential references only; never persist or export a plaintext API key.
Support session memory, environment variables, optional OS keyring, and no-auth local providers.
Run the same prompt against multiple OpenAI-compatible providers and retain deterministic comparable results.
Redact credentials from transport failures and result exports, including reflected values.
Provide tests, security documentation, Windows launch instructions, and a GUI smoke check.

quality_metrics.measure: headless GUI startup and tab render

prevention: Keep credentials behind a SecretManager boundary and restrict persisted authentication metadata to allowlisted values.
Force keyring and session references to equal provider_id so the reference cannot become a hidden key field.
Require HTTPS for all non-local endpoints.
assurance: Exercise configuration, secret resolution, redaction, adapter transport, comparison ordering, export, packaging, and GUI startup.
control: Make no paid provider call and do not modify the production Provider route.
improvement: Add protocol-specific adapters only through the registry while preserving the same credential and redaction boundaries.

interface_expectations: The extension is a local experiment surface, not a second production generation route.
ProviderJob remains the only canonical project-work Provider boundary.
local_packager remains the only delivery exit.
The GUI may compare model responses but cannot grant formal project or release PASS.
Provider configuration exports metadata only and comparison exports omit credential location fields.

feedback: The extension is isolated from the production route and uses only standard-library runtime dependencies.
Plaintext credential persistence and export are rejected or redacted by tested boundaries.
Live provider behavior and Windows keyring integration remain NOT_EVALUATED until the user supplies local credentials.

worked: OpenAI-compatible providers share one adapter while presets remain editable.
Session, environment, keyring, and no-auth modes cover local testing without a plaintext fallback file.
The GUI and headless service share the same validated configuration and result contracts.
did_not_work: An initial generic string trim removed the space from the Bearer prefix; a focused transport test exposed and closed it.
An initial result export relied only on adapter redaction; export-time credential scrubbing was added as defense in depth.
experiments: Use this lab to compare providers on a frozen prompt set before changing the canonical Provider profile.
Add native non-OpenAI protocols only after a concrete provider requires them.
